findings.rule: PRD 10.5 dynamic text size; Prototype.dc.html:835: the toggle row is an unclipped full-width button, and the card supplies padding 0 16px
findings.trigger: The Fixer clips the whole full-width row to TmrTheme.shapes.pill, which is CircleShape. The label Text starts at x=0 with no horizontal padding. Take TmrToggle(label = "Email me when a tailored application is ready to review") in a 374 dp column, or any label at font scale 2.0. The label wraps to 2 lines, so the row is 48 dp tall and the corner radius is 24 dp. At the cap top of line 1 (y about 7 dp), the clip edge is at x about 7 dp, so the top-left of the first glyph is cut off. The same happens to the bottom-left of line 2, and taller rows cut more. At 1.0, the single-line 'Notify me' baseline is intact, which is why the baselines miss this. Fix: drop the row clip, or clip to a shape whose radius is no larger than the horizontal padding (for example pillRow with padding of 16 dp or more).
findings.title: Pill clip on the toggle row cuts the leading glyphs of a wrapped label
findings.proof: Add a Roborazzi capture of TmrToggle with a two-line label at TmrTestDevices.prototypeLargeFont. The first glyph is visibly cut. Alternatively, sample the pixels of the first glyph column at the line-1 cap top and compare them with the same composable without .clip.

findings.rule: Review checklist 1: the test must fail if the fix is reverted (round-1 headline truncation)
findings.trigger: Compose's FontScaling uses nonlinear scaling at fontScale 2.0. 28 sp becomes about 37 dp, not 56 dp: the glyphs in hero_card_blue_font200 are about 1.32x the 1.0 baseline. So 'Tell Paige about you' at 374 dp wraps to exactly 2 lines, and the baseline shows 'Tell Paige / about you'. If maxLines = 2 and TextOverflow.Ellipsis are restored, hasVisualOverflow stays false and this test and the new baseline both still pass. My round-1 trigger assumed linear 56 sp. The fix is still correct, because longer headlines exceed 2 lines even at 1.0, but nothing guards it.
findings.title: Font-2.0 headline test passes on the pre-fix code
findings.proof: Revert TmrHeroCard to maxLines = 2 with overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis. headlineFullyDisplayedAtFontScale200 still passes. Use the long headline from headlineStyle and assert lineCount > 2 and !hasVisualOverflow. That test fails on the old code.
